Bamboo flutes have a long history in China and India, and the transverse flute reached Europe by way of Byzantium and Germany. The nineteenth-century flute grew out of the German flute, and Theobald Boehm developed his key system between 1832 and 1847, extending the range and improving intonation.

The recorder was a standard solo instrument in the Baroque era, and the simple plastic recorder is common in primary and secondary school music teaching today. The Chinese di is used in Chinese orchestra music; the Korean daegeum, junggeum and sogeum are known together as the three bamboo flutes and are traditional instruments of the Silla period. Japanese flutes include the nōkan; the sring is used in the Caucasus region of Armenia, and the Indian bansuri is associated with religious art and with the image of Krishna.
長笛屬橫笛，吹奏時笛身與嘴唇平行，以氣流掠過側面吹口，使吹口處空氣振動發聲。初學: The flute is a side-blown instrument: the tube lies parallel to the lips and the airstream passes over the blowing edge at the side, setting the air at the edge vibrating. A beginner first settles the position of the blowing edge, then opens and closes the holes to change the length of the resonating tube and get different pitches; the key system lets one finger control several linked holes at once. For breathing, use the diaphragm to take in enough air and to keep the playing from breaking off; more advanced players practise circular breathing, breathing in through the nose while pushing air out through the mouth.
長笛屬邊稜音樂器，氣流掠過吹口使管內空氣柱振動；開閉音孔改變有效管長與共振頻率，: The flute is an edge-blown instrument: the airstream passes the blowing edge and sets the air column in the tube vibrating; opening and closing the holes changes the effective length of the tube and its resonant frequency, and raising the air pressure lets the air resonate on a harmonic rather than the fundamental. The flute's timbre is brighter and richer in overtones; its range runs from middle C to the third C above, three octaves. The piccolo sounds an octave higher, and the alto and bass flutes lower. Unlike the recorder and other whistle flutes, the flute sounds at a side-blown edge; compared with end-blown flutes such as the xiao, it is held across the face. The player directs the airstream across the side blowing edge, setting the air column in the tube vibrating; the usual construction is a side-blown tube closed at the far end, with a blowing edge and holes or keys for setting the pitch, made mostly of metal today, with a range of about three octaves. The flute is blown by a flute player and belongs to the wind instruments; the piccolo, alto flute and bass flute are variants of the family.
